newsitem.title: CANADA: Viking replica ship to be towed back to Greenland.
newsitem.headline: Viking replica ship to be towed back to Greenland.

text.p: A malfunctioning rudder has ended the attempt to sail a replica of a 1,000-year-old Viking ship to Canada from Greenland, the Canadian Press news agency said on Sunday.
The agency said the Canadian Coast Guard took the Snorri under tow because of rudder problems, breaking plans to re-create Leif Ericsson's voyage from Greenland to Canada.
The ship was intercepted about 169 miles (272 km) from Greenland after the crew reported rudder problems, said a spokesman for the Rescue Co-ordination Center in Halifax.

A Danish rescue vessel was to take over the towing later on Sunday and the 52-foot (15.9 metre) Snorri was to be back at its original port of Nuuk, Greenland, by about 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), the Center said.

The Snorri began its voyage on Aug. 8. Its planned destination was to have been L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland. The trip, which was to have taken six to eight weeks and cost hundreds of thousands of dollars, was sponsored by Land's End, a mail-order clothing company in Wisconsin.
